clue.text: French port receiving a quantity of chicken

indicators.note: a port receiving something takes it in, so the port's name holds the letter within it

parts.note: Brest is a port in Brittany, France

explanation.surface: A Breton harbour taking delivery of a consignment of poultry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' looks like part of 'a quantity of chicken' but is the letter A that Brest takes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Breast is a cut of white meat from a bird, a portion one buys or serves.

clue.text: Wasting time, I exported nasty bleach

indicators.note: something nasty is in a bad, mangled state, so these letters are rearranged
wasting time means losing it, so that letter is dropped from the words

explanation.surface: Someone frets that shipping a harsh chemical abroad cost them hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasting' drops T from I EXPORTED, leaving IEXPORED; 'nasty' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydrogen peroxide is a common bleaching agent, especially for hair.

clue.text: Fixed line limiting height for Jewish settlement

indicators.note: to limit something is to hem it in, so these letters enclose the other

parts.note: stet, 'let it stand', is the proofreader's mark telling the printer a word stays fixed as it was

explanation.surface: A rule fixing a maximum building height, applied to a village.
explanation.walkthrough: STET is a proofreading instruction to leave text unchanged; H sits inside STET + L just after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A shtetl was a small Jewish town or village in Eastern Europe before the Holocaust.

clue.text: Obsessive year is involving special research

parts.note: anal, informally, means obsessively fussy

indicators.note: to involve is to take in, so these letters wrap around the other

explanation.surface: A fixated person spends a whole year on a particular study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' sets S between Y and IS, making YSIS.
explanation.definitionFit: An analysis is a detailed examination, the kind of careful study research consists of.

clue.text: Elects Conservative — I'm sorry about that ultimately

indicators.note: about here means around, so one word wraps the following letter

parts.note: oops is a quick apology for a slip

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word that

explanation.surface: A voter backs the Tory and then apologises for it.
explanation.definitionFit: To co-opt is to elect someone into a body by the votes of its existing members.

clue.text: Unusual stir about hackneyed items, things in the 'old hat' category?

indicators.note: about means around, so the scrambled letters surround the other piece
unusual signals an odd new order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: corn is trite, sentimental material, hence 'corny'

explanation.surface: Someone stirs up a fuss over clichés that are out of fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' turns STIR into TRIS, which goes 'about' CORN. 'Old hat' means outdated, but the definition reads it literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Tricorns are three-cornered hats of the eighteenth century, literally old hats.

clue.text: Perhaps add water to ferns here, wilting

indicators.note: wilting plants droop out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener suggests watering the drooping ferns in this spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To refreshen is to restore freshness, and watering is one way, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Evidence of an out-of-this-world domestic bust-up?

definitions.text: Evidence of an out-of-this-world domestic bust-up?

parts.words: Evidence of an out-of-this-world domestic bust-up?
parts.note: in a marital row crockery gets thrown through the air; supposed alien craft are named after that same crockery

explanation.surface: A tabloid hint of a cosmic marital row.
explanation.walkthrough: Read one way, it is crockery hurled in a domestic fight; read another, UFO sightings.
explanation.definitionFit: Flying saucers are reported alien spacecraft, and also, literally, saucers thrown in a quarrel.

clue.text: Different person subject to order, abandoned by British

indicators.note: being abandoned by something means it leaves, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: a brother is a member of a religious order

explanation.surface: A disciplined underling is left behind by the British.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' suggests commands, but here it means a monastic order.
explanation.definitionFit: Other means distinct or not the same, a plain synonym of different.

clue.text: Grass needing protection with snug covering in Sussex town

parts.note: hay is dried grass
ward means guard or protection, as in 'ward off'
a sheath is a close-fitting cover

explanation.surface: Lawn needing shelter under a cosy cover, somewhere in the south of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Haywards Heath is a commuter town in West Sussex, a county on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Haywards Heath is a real town in West Sussex, England, so it is an example of the category.

clue.text: US city enveloped in love for Little Italy in the future

indicators.note: being enveloped in something means being wrapped inside it

parts.note: amore is Italian for love, the language of New York's Little Italy district
NY is New York

explanation.surface: New York wrapped in affection for its Italian quarter.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Italy is the Italian neighbourhood of New York, which is why the Italian word for love is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Any more, as in 'not any more', means from now on, so it refers to time to come.

clue.text: Head off bits of film by Young Conservatives adopting new dubbing technique

indicators.note: taking off the head means the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: clips are short excerpts of film

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so these letters hold the next one

parts.note: YC stands for the Young Conservatives, the Tory youth wing

explanation.surface: Footage from a youth political group is beheaded and redubbed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Young Conservatives are the youth wing of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Lip-syncing matches mouth movements to a recorded soundtrack, a staple of dubbing.

clue.text: Began list laying out these assets?

indicators.note: laying out means arranging afresh, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone starts an inventory of their physical holdings.
explanation.walkthrough: The list one would lay out is of physical possessions, so the definition depends on the rest of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangibles are assets with physical substance, as opposed to intangibles such as goodwill.

clue.text: Commotion surrounding American element of flight

indicators.note: surrounding means going round, so these letters enclose the other

parts.note: a stir is a fuss or commotion

explanation.surface: Uproar breaks out around an American during an air journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests aeroplanes but means a flight of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of stairs is made up of individual steps, each one being a single unit of it.

clue.text: Restrained but losing head in hurry

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: chaste means restrained or modest

explanation.surface: Someone stays composed but cracks when rushed.
explanation.definitionFit: Haste is speed or urgency, the noun matching hurry as in 'in a hurry'.

clue.text: Corner resident nearly securing spot for dance

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so these letters enclose the other
nearly means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: Little Jack Horner, of the nursery rhyme, sat in a corner
a pip is a spot, as on dice or cards

explanation.surface: Someone living on a street corner claims a place to dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme 'Little Jack Horner sat in the corner' explains the resident; HORNE holds PIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A hornpipe is a lively solo dance traditionally associated with sailors.

clue.text: Vehicle not working? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite the whole word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: bust means broken, not working

explanation.surface: A broken-down vehicle — or nearly.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus is a large road vehicle carrying passengers.

clue.text: Lizard I left is found in lounge

indicators.note: being found in something means lying inside it

parts.note: to bask is to lounge in the sun

explanation.surface: A pet reptile is abandoned in the sitting room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lounge' reads as a room but is the verb to bask.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides the mythical serpent, a basilisk is a real Central American lizard that can run on water.

clue.text: Line is circling party venues supporting swimming

indicators.note: circling means going round, so these letters surround the other

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: A queue snakes around a party at the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A lido is a public open-air swimming pool, or a bathing beach.

clue.text: Position King overlooked in a certain European subject

parts.note: a lie is a position, as in 'the lie of the land'

indicators.note: overlooked means left out, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a German is a European of one particular nation
R is for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A European monarch's place is ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subject' is a noun here: one who owes allegiance.
explanation.definitionFit: A liegeman is a vassal sworn to serve a feudal lord, thus a monarch's subject.

clue.text: Severe depression doing head in

indicators.note: doing in the head means killing off the first letter

parts.note: a trough is a depression, in land or in weather

explanation.surface: Deep gloom is driving someone mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doing head in' is slang for annoying, but here it means removing the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough treatment or weather is harsh, so rough can stand for severe.

clue.text: A lot of mist on a road is a concern for drivers

indicators.note: a lot of a word is most but not all of it, so its last letter goes

parts.note: haze is a light mist

explanation.surface: Fog on the highway worries motorists.
explanation.walkthrough: The drivers are golfers: a hazard is a bunker or water obstacle on a course.
explanation.definitionFit: A hazard is a danger generally, and in golf an obstacle that worries those hitting long tee shots.

clue.text: Setter accommodating pilots aboard special flying machine

indicators.note: being aboard is being inside the vessel, so these letters go within the other piece
accommodating means housing, so these letters surround the other

parts.note: Phi is the pseudonym of this puzzle's setter
aces are expert fighter pilots

explanation.surface: The puzzle's author puts up some airmen on a special aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: Phi is this puzzle's setter, so 'Setter' gives his pseudonym; 'accommodating' gives PACESHI, which goes 'aboard' the two letters for special.
explanation.definitionFit: A spaceship is a craft that travels through space, a machine that flies.

clue.text: Foreigners giving misinformation in answer

indicators.note: in places the first piece within the second

parts.note: a lie is misinformation

explanation.surface: Visitors from abroad give a false reply.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliens are people who are not citizens of the country they live in.

clue.text: Carefully examine including old film as example of literature

indicators.note: including means containing, so these letters enclose the others

parts.note: to pry is to look closely and inquisitively
ET is Spielberg's 1982 film

explanation.surface: Scrutinise a classic movie as a literary work.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetry is one form of literature, alongside prose and drama.

clue.text: French ready with enthusiasm to dismiss a German cracker

parts.note: prêt is French for ready

indicators.note: to dismiss is to send away, so that letter is removed

parts.note: zeal is enthusiasm

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is keen to sack a German comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracker' suggests a joke or a stunner; it is a crisp snack.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretzel is a knotted, crisp baked snack originating in southern Germany.

clue.text: Learned to ignore first repeat

indicators.note: ignoring the first means the word's opening letter is dropped

parts.note: literate means learned, well read

explanation.surface: A scholar was taught to overlook the opening.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to do or say again, so it is a synonym of repeat.

clue.text: Increasingly aristocratic, avoiding hard question

indicators.note: avoiding means steering clear of, so that letter is left out

parts.note: posher means more upper-class
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A social climber dodges a tricky inquiry.
explanation.definitionFit: A poser is a puzzling or difficult problem.

clue.text: Unusual heat burns — me?

indicators.note: unusual signals a strange order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone scorched by a freak heatwave asks who they are.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: the person who gets burnt in rare heat is the one lying in the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunbather lies out in sunshine and risks sunburn when the heat is unusually strong.
